newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Matches scheduled for Wednesday in the English premier league (kick-off times 1945 GMT unless stated, league positions in parentheses):

Chelsea player-coach Ruud Gullit will be in plaster for a month after breaking his ankle in the 3-2 defeat by Derby on Saturday. Italian striker Gianfranco Zola returns after being rested to help the London club's chances of a European place, while Norwegian Frode Grodas will again stand in for injured goalkeeper Kevin Hitchcock. Midfielder Eddie Newton is likely to be out for two weeks after undergoing a cartilage operation but defenders Dan Petrescu and Erland Johnsen and midfielder Craig Burley should be fit.

Blackburn have taken seven out of nine points in their rise to premier league safety, including a 1-0 win over Sunderland on Saturday. They are likely to welcome back striker Chris Sutton after illness. Greek winger George Donis is doubtful with an ankle injury.

Aston Villa put a dent in Liverpool's title challenge with a 1-0 win on Sunday and are now strong contenders for a European berth next season after three wins in their last four games. Defender David Hughes is on standby to replace ankle injury victim Steve Staunton. Villa will be hoping to move above Newcastle in the league with a victory over local rivals Leicester who beat Wimbledon 3-1 on Saturday.
Middlesbrough's relegation worries increased in a 3-1 defeat by Sheffield Wednesday. Defender Derek Whyte will be out with a hamstring injury in an otherwise unchanged squad.

Derby caused a surprise with a well-earned 3-2 victory over Chelsea last Saturday and coach Jim Smith is likely to name an unchanged squad. Defender Chris Powell could be on the substitutes' bench after missing the last two games with an ankle injury, while midfielder Paul Trollope serves the second match of a two-game ban. Striker Dean Sturridge plays his last game before starting a two-match suspension this Saturday.

Nottingham Forest, who beat Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, welcome the return of Mark Crossley in goal against a Sheffield Wednesday side who have lost only once in 21 games. Midfielder Ian Woan serves the second of a two-match ban while midfielder Chris Bart-Williams (knee) and striker Kevin Campbell (hamstring) are doubtful.
Sheffield Wednesday coach David Pleat has a fully fit squad available. Regi Blinker plays his final game before starting a two-match ban.

Southampton helped their fight for premier league safety with a 1-0 win at Newcastle and coach Graeme Souness has defenders Jason Dodd and Ken Monkou back in first-team contention in what should be an otherwise unchanged side.

Everton's disappointing form continued when they were beaten 2-0 by Arsenal last Saturday. They have won only once in their last nine games. Coach Joe Royle has taken Monaco midfielder Lauren Viaud on a week's trial and Welsh goalkeeper Neville Southall will start in place of calf victim Paul Gerrard. Midfielder Tony Grant is still out with a knee problem.
